exampleAnswers.title: Calculating the Volume of a Parallelepiped Spanned by Three Vectors

question.text: Compute the volume $V$ of the parallelepiped spanned by the vectors $\mathbf{p} = \langle 1, 0, 5 \rangle$, $\mathbf{q} = \langle 3, 2, 6 \rangle$, and $\mathbf{r} = \langle 0, 4, 1 \rangle.$
question.explanation:
The volume of a parallelepiped spanned by three vectors is given by the absolute value of their triple product.

First, we compute the triple product:

\begin{align*} \mathbf{p} \cdot (\mathbf{q} \times \mathbf{r})& = \left\lvert \begin{array}{ccc} 1 & 0 & 5 \\ 3 & 2 & 6 \\ 0 & 4 & 1 \end{array} \right\rvert\\[5pt] &= 1 \cdot \left\lvert \begin{array}{cc} 2 & 6 \\ 4 & 1 \end{array} \right\rvert - 0 \cdot \left\lvert \begin{array}{cc} 3 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 \end{array} \right\rvert + 5 \cdot \left\lvert \begin{array}{cc} 3 & 2 \\ 0 & 4 \end{array} \right\rvert \\[5pt] &= 1(2 \cdot 1 - 6 \cdot 4) + 0 + 5(3 \cdot 4 - 2 \cdot 0) \\[5pt] &= -22 + 60 \\[5pt] &= 38 \end{align*}

Finally, we take the absolute value. So, the volume of the corresponding parallelepiped is

\[ V = |38| = \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{38}. \]

question.text: Compute the volume $V$ of the parallelepiped spanned by the vectors $\mathbf{x} = \langle 2, 3, 0 \rangle$, $\mathbf{y} = \langle 1, 4, 5 \rangle$, and $\mathbf{z} = \langle 0, 2, 6 \rangle.$
question.explanation:
The volume of a parallelepiped spanned by three vectors is given by the absolute value of their triple product.

First, we compute the triple product:

\begin{align*} \mathbf{x} \cdot (\mathbf{y} \times \mathbf{z}) &= \left\lvert \begin{array}{ccc} 2 & 3 & 0 \\ 1 & 4 & 5 \\ 0 & 2 & 6 \end{array} \right\rvert\\[5pt] &= 2 \cdot \left\lvert \begin{array}{cc} 4 & 5 \\ 2 & 6 \end{array} \right\rvert - 3 \cdot \left\lvert \begin{array}{cc} 1 & 5 \\ 0 & 6 \end{array} \right\rvert + 0 \cdot \left\lvert \begin{array}{cc} 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 2 \end{array} \right\rvert \\[5pt] &= 2(4 \cdot 6 - 5 \cdot 2) - 3(1 \cdot 6 - 5 \cdot 0) + 0 \\[5pt] &= 2(24 - 10) - 3(6)\\[5pt] &= 28 - 18\\[5pt] & = 10 \end{align*}

Finally, we take the absolute value. So, the volume of the corresponding parallelepiped is

\[ V = |10| = \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{10}. \]

question.text: Calculate the volume of the parallelepiped spanned by $\mathbf{a}=\langle -3,3,1 \rangle$, $\mathbf{b}=\langle 2,-1,3 \rangle$ and $\mathbf{c}=\langle 0,4,1 \rangle.$
question.explanation:
The volume of the parallelepiped spanned by three vectors is given by the absolute value of their triple product.

First, we compute the triple product:

\begin{align*} \mathbf{a} \cdot (\mathbf{b} \times \mathbf{c}) & = \left \lvert \begin{array}{ccc} -3 & 3 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 3 \\ 0 & 4 & 1 \end{array} \right\lvert \\[5pt] &=(-3)\cdot \left \lvert \begin{array}{cc} -1 & 3 \\ 4 & 1 \end{array} \right\lvert - 3\cdot \left \lvert \begin{array}{cc} 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 \end{array} \right\lvert +1\cdot \left \lvert \begin{array}{cc} 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 4 \end{array} \right\lvert\\[5pt] &= -3 ((-1)\cdot 1 - 4\cdot 3) - 3(2\cdot 1 - 0\cdot 3)+(2\cdot 4 -0\cdot (-1))\\[5pt] &= 39-6+8\\[5pt] &=41 \end{align*}

Finally, we take the absolute value. So the volume of the corresponding parallelepiped is

\[ V=|41|=41. \]

question.text: Compute the volume $V$ of the parallelepiped spanned by the vectors $\mathbf{a} = \langle 1, 2, 3 \rangle$, $\mathbf{b} = \langle 0, 5, 0 \rangle$, and $\mathbf{c} = \langle 4, 0, 6 \rangle.$
question.explanation:
The volume of a parallelepiped spanned by three vectors is given by the absolute value of their triple product.

First, we compute the triple product:

\begin{align*} \mathbf{a} \cdot (\mathbf{b} \times \mathbf{c}) &= \left\lvert \begin{array}{ccc} 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 5 & 0 \\ 4 & 0 & 6 \end{array} \right\rvert\\[5pt] &= 1 \cdot \left\lvert \begin{array}{cc} 5 & 0 \\ 0 & 6 \end{array} \right\rvert - 2 \cdot \left\lvert \begin{array}{cc} 0 & 0 \\ 4 & 6 \end{array} \right\rvert + 3 \cdot \left\lvert \begin{array}{cc} 0 & 5 \\ 4 & 0 \end{array} \right\rvert \\[5pt] &= 1(30) - 2(0) + 3(-20) \\[5pt] & = 30 - 0 - 60\\[5pt] & = -30 \end{align*}

Finally, we take the absolute value. So, the volume of the corresponding parallelepiped is

\[ V = |{-30}| = \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{30}. \]

question.text: Calculate the volume of the parallelepiped spanned by $\mathbf{p}=\langle 0,1,-1 \rangle$, $\mathbf{q}=\langle -2,3,1 \rangle$ and $\mathbf{r}=\langle -1,4,3 \rangle.$
question.explanation:
The volume of the parallelepiped spanned by three vectors is given by the absolute value of their triple product.

First, we compute the triple product:

\begin{align*} \mathbf{p} \cdot (\mathbf{q} \times \mathbf{r}) &= \left \lvert \begin{array}{ccc} 0 & 1 & -1 \\ -2 & 3 & 1 \\ -1 & 4 & 3 \end{array} \right\lvert\\[5pt] &=0 \cdot \left \lvert \begin{array}{cc} 3 & 1 \\ 4 & 3 \end{array} \right\lvert -1 \cdot \left \lvert \begin{array}{cc} -2 & 1 \\ -1 & 3 \end{array} \right\lvert +(-1)\cdot \left \lvert \begin{array}{cc} -2 & 3 \\ -1 & 4 \end{array} \right\lvert\\[5pt] &= 0- ((-2)\cdot 3 - (-1)\cdot 1)- ((-2)\cdot 4 - (-1)\cdot 3)\\[5pt] &= 5+5\\[5pt] &=10 \end{align*}

Finally, we take the absolute value. So the volume of the corresponding parallelepiped is \[ V=|10|=10. \]

exampleAnswers.title: Determining Whether Three Vectors are Coplanar

question.text: Find $t$ given that the vectors ${\mathbf{p}}=\langle t,1,t \rangle$, ${\mathbf{q}}=\langle 2,-1,-1 \rangle$, and ${\bf{r}}=\langle 3,0,1 \rangle$ are coplanar.
question.explanation:
Computing the triple product, we get

\begin{align*} \mathbf{p} \cdot (\mathbf{q} \times \mathbf{r}) &= \left \lvert \begin{array}{ccc} t & 1 & t \\ 2 & -1 & -1 \\ 3 & 0 & 1 \end{array} \right\lvert \\[5pt] &=t \cdot \left \lvert \begin{array}{cc} -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 \end{array} \right\lvert - 1 \cdot \left \lvert \begin{array}{cc} 2 & -1 \\ 3 & 1 \end{array} \right\lvert +t \cdot \left \lvert \begin{array}{cc} 2 & -1 \\ 3 & 0 \end{array} \right\lvert\\[5pt] &= t\left((-1)\cdot 1 - 0\cdot (-1)\right) - \left(2 \cdot 1 - 3 \cdot (-1)\right) + t\left(2 \cdot 0 - 3 \cdot (-1)\right) \\[5pt] &= -t -5 +3t \\[5pt] &=2t-5. \end{align*}

Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their triple product is zero:

\begin{align*} \mathbf{p} \cdot (\mathbf{q} \times \mathbf{r}) &= 0 \\[3pt] 2t-5 &= 0 \\[3pt] 2t &= 5 \\[3pt] t &= \dfrac 5 2 \end{align*}

Therefore, the three vectors are coplanar if and only if $t=\dfrac 5 2.$

example.title: Determining Whether Three Vectors are Coplanar

question.text: Find $k$ given that the vectors $\mathbf{a}=\langle k,k,2 \rangle$, $\mathbf{b}=\langle 1,3,0 \rangle$, and $\mathbf{c}=\langle 0,4,5 \rangle$ are coplanar.
question.explanation:
Computing the triple product, we get

\begin{align*} \mathbf{a} \cdot (\mathbf{b} \times \mathbf{c}) &= \left \lvert \begin{array}{ccc} k & k & 2 \\ 1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 5 \end{array} \right\lvert \\[5pt] &= k \cdot \left \lvert \begin{array}{cc} 3 & 0 \\ 4 & 5 \end{array} \right\rvert - k \cdot \left \lvert \begin{array}{cc} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 \end{array} \right\rvert + 2 \cdot \left \lvert \begin{array}{cc} 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 4 \end{array} \right\rvert\\[5pt] &= k(3 \cdot 5 - 0 \cdot 4) - k(1 \cdot 5 - 0 \cdot 0) + 2(1 \cdot 4 - 3 \cdot 0) \\[5pt] &= k(15) - k(5) + 2(4) \\[5pt] &= 15k - 5k + 8 \\[5pt] &= 10k + 8 \end{align*}

Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their triple product is zero:

\begin{align*} \mathbf{a} \cdot (\mathbf{b} \times \mathbf{c}) &= 0 \\[5pt] 10k + 8 &= 0 \\[5pt] 10k &= -8 \\[5pt] k &= -\dfrac{4}{5} \end{align*}

Therefore, the three vectors are coplanar if and only if $k=\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{{-\dfrac{4}{5}}}.$

example.title: Determining Whether Three Vectors are Coplanar

question.text: Find $k$ given that the vectors $\mathbf{a}=\langle 1,k,k \rangle$, $\mathbf{b}=\langle 0,3,2 \rangle$, and $\mathbf{c}=\langle 4,0,5 \rangle$ are coplanar.
question.explanation:
Computing the triple product, we get

\begin{align*} \mathbf{a} \cdot (\mathbf{b} \times \mathbf{c}) &= \left \lvert \begin{array}{ccc} 1 & k & k \\ 0 & 3 & 2 \\ 4 & 0 & 5 \end{array} \right\lvert \\[5pt] &= 1 \cdot \left \lvert \begin{array}{cc} 3 & 2 \\ 0 & 5 \end{array} \right\rvert - k \cdot \left \lvert \begin{array}{cc} 0 & 2 \\ 4 & 5 \end{array} \right\rvert + k \cdot \left \lvert \begin{array}{cc} 0 & 3 \\ 4 & 0 \end{array} \right\rvert\\[5pt] &= 1(3 \cdot 5 - 2 \cdot 0) - k(0 \cdot 5 - 2 \cdot 4) + k(0 \cdot 0 - 3 \cdot 4) \\[5pt] & = 15 + 8k - 12k \\[5pt] &= 15 - 4k \end{align*}

Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their triple product is zero:

\begin{align*} \mathbf{a} \cdot (\mathbf{b} \times \mathbf{c}) &= 0 \\[5pt] 15 - 4k &= 0 \\[5pt] 4k &= 15 \\[5pt] k &= \frac{15}{4} \end{align*}

Therefore, the three vectors are coplanar if and only if $k=\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{{\dfrac{15}{4}}}.$

example.title: Determining Whether Three Vectors are Coplanar

question.text: Find $k$ given that the vectors $\mathbf{a}=\langle k,1,4 \rangle,$ $\mathbf{b}=\langle 8,0,3 \rangle,$ and $\mathbf{c}=\langle 3,1,1 \rangle$ are coplanar.
question.explanation:
Computing the triple product, we get

\begin{align*} \mathbf{a} \cdot (\mathbf{b} \times \mathbf{c}) &= \left \lvert \begin{array}{ccc} k & 1 & 4 \\ 8 & 0 & 3 \\ 3 & 1 & 1 \end{array} \right\lvert \\[5pt] &=k \cdot \left \lvert \begin{array}{cc} 0 & 3 \\ 1 & 1 \end{array} \right\lvert - 1 \cdot \left \lvert \begin{array}{cc} 8 & 3 \\ 3 & 1 \end{array} \right\lvert + 4 \cdot \left \lvert \begin{array}{cc} 8 & 0 \\ 3 & 1 \end{array} \right\lvert\\[5pt] &= k\left(0 \cdot 1 - 1 \cdot 3\right) - \left(8 \cdot 1 - 3 \cdot 3\right) + 4\left(8 \cdot 1 - 3 \cdot 0\right) \\[5pt] &= -3k+1+32\\[5pt] &=33-3k\\[5pt] &=3(11-k). \end{align*}

Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their triple product is zero:

\begin{align*} \mathbf{a} \cdot (\mathbf{b} \times \mathbf{c}) &= 0 \\[5pt] 3(11-k) &= 0 \\[5pt] 11-k &= 0 \\[5pt] k &= 11 \end{align*}

Therefore, the three vectors are coplanar if and only if $k=11.$

question.text: Find $k$ given that the vectors $\mathbf{a}=\langle k,2,2 \rangle$, $\mathbf{b}=\langle 3,0,2 \rangle$ and $\mathbf{c}=\langle 4,1,3 \rangle$ are coplanar.
question.explanation:
Computing the triple product, we get

\begin{align*} \mathbf{a} \cdot (\mathbf{b} \times \mathbf{c}) & = \left \lvert \begin{array}{ccc} k & 2 & 2 \\ 3 & 0 & 2 \\ 4 & 1 & 3 \end{array} \right\lvert \\[5pt] &=k \cdot \left \lvert \begin{array}{cc} 0 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 \end{array} \right\lvert - 2\cdot \left \lvert \begin{array}{cc} 3 & 2 \\ 4 & 3 \end{array} \right\lvert + 2\cdot \left \lvert \begin{array}{cc} 3 & 0 \\ 4 & 1 \end{array} \right\lvert\\[5pt] &= k(0\cdot 3 - 1\cdot 2) - 2(3\cdot 3 - 4\cdot 2)+ 2(3\cdot 1 -4\cdot 0)\\[5pt] &= -2k-2+6\\[5pt] &= -2k+4. \end{align*}

Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their triple product is zero:

\begin{align*} \mathbf{a} \cdot (\mathbf{b} \times \mathbf{c}) &= 0 \\[5pt] -2k+4 &= 0 \\[5pt] 2k &= 4 \\[5pt] k &= 2 \end{align*}

Therefore, the three vectors are coplanar if and only if $k=2.$

exampleAnswers.title: Calculating the Volume of a Parallelepiped Spanned by Three Position Vectors Given Their Coordinates

question.text: Calculate the volume $V$ of the parallelepiped spanned by $\overrightarrow{AB},$ $\overrightarrow{AC},$ and $\overrightarrow{AD},$ given the points $A(0,1,3),$ $B(0,5,5),$ $C(3,4,5),$ and $D(2,0,2).$
question.explanation:
First, we find the displacement vectors $\overrightarrow{AB},$ $\overrightarrow{AC},$ and $\overrightarrow{AD}$ that span the parallelepiped:

\begin{align*} \overrightarrow{AB} &= \mathbf{b}-\mathbf{a} \\[3pt] &= (5\mathbf{j}+5\mathbf{k})-(1\mathbf{j}+3\mathbf{k}) \\[3pt] &= 4\mathbf{j}+2\mathbf{k} \\[3pt] &= \langle 0,4,2 \rangle \\[7pt] \overrightarrow{AC} &= \mathbf{c}-\mathbf{a} \\[3pt] &= (3\mathbf{i}+4\mathbf{j}+5\mathbf{k})-(1\mathbf{j}+3\mathbf{k}) \\[3pt] &= 3\mathbf{i}+3\mathbf{j}+2\mathbf{k} \\[3pt] &= \langle 3,3,2 \rangle \\[7pt] \overrightarrow{AD} &= \mathbf{d}-\mathbf{a} \\[3pt] &= (2\mathbf{i}+2\mathbf{k})-(1\mathbf{j}+3\mathbf{k}) \\[3pt] &= 2\mathbf{i}-1\mathbf{j}-1\mathbf{k} \\[3pt] &= \langle 2,-1,-1 \rangle \end{align*}

Now, to find the volume of the parallelepiped, we need to take the absolute value of the triple product of the above vectors.

Computing the triple product, we have

\begin{align*} \overrightarrow{AB} \cdot (\overrightarrow{AC} \times \overrightarrow{AD}) &= \left| \begin{array}{ccc} 0 & 4 & 2 \\ 3 & 3 & 2 \\ 2 & -1 & -1 \end{array} \right| \\[5pt] &= 0 \cdot \left| \begin{array}{cc} 3 & 2 \\ -1 & -1 \end{array} \right| - 4 \cdot \left| \begin{array}{cc} 3 & 2 \\ 2 & -1 \end{array} \right| + 2 \cdot \left| \begin{array}{cc} 3 & 3 \\ 2 & -1 \end{array} \right| \\[5pt] &= -4(3 \cdot -1 - 2 \cdot 2) + 2(3 \cdot -1 - 3 \cdot 2) \\[5pt] &= 28 - 18\\[5pt] &= 10. \end{align*}

Therefore, the volume of the corresponding parallelepiped spanned by $\overrightarrow{AB},$ $\overrightarrow{AC},$ and $\overrightarrow{AD}$ is \[ V = |10| = \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{10}. \]

question.text: Calculate the volume of the parallelepiped spanned by $\overrightarrow{AB}$, $\overrightarrow{AC}$ and $\overrightarrow{AD}$, given the points $A(1,-1,2)$, $B(-2,2,3)$, $C(1,1,1)$, and $D(-1,3,-2).$
question.explanation:
First, we find the displacement vectors $\overrightarrow{AB},$ $\overrightarrow{AC},$ and $\overrightarrow{AD}$ that span the parallelepiped:

\begin{align*} \overrightarrow{AB} &= \mathbf{b}-\mathbf{a} \\[3pt] &= (-2\mathbf{i}+2\mathbf{j}+3\mathbf{k})-(\mathbf{i}-\mathbf{j}+2\mathbf{k}) \\[3pt] &= -3\mathbf{i}+3\mathbf{j}+\mathbf{k} \\[3pt] &= \langle -3,3,1 \rangle \\[7pt] \overrightarrow{AC} &= \mathbf{c}-\mathbf{a} \\[3pt] &= (\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j}+\mathbf{k})-(\mathbf{i}-\mathbf{j}+2\mathbf{k}) \\[3pt] &= 2\mathbf{j}-\mathbf{k} \\[3pt] &= \langle 0,2,-1 \rangle \\[7pt] \overrightarrow{AD} &= \mathbf{d}-\mathbf{a} \\[3pt] &= (-\mathbf{i}+3\mathbf{j}-2\mathbf{k})-(\mathbf{i}-\mathbf{j}+2\mathbf{k}) \\[3pt] &= -2\mathbf{i}+4\mathbf{j}-4\mathbf{k} \\[3pt] &= \langle -2,4,-4 \rangle \end{align*}

Now, to find the volume of the parallelepiped, we need to take the absolute value of the triple product of the above vectors.

Computing the triple product, we have

\begin{align*} \overrightarrow{AB} \cdot (\overrightarrow{AC} \times \overrightarrow{AD}) &= \left| \begin{array}{ccc} -3 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & -1 \\ -2 & 4 & -4 \end{array} \right| \\[5pt] &= (-3) \cdot \left| \begin{array}{cc} 2 & -1 \\ 4 & -4 \end{array} \right| - 3 \cdot \left| \begin{array}{cc} 0 & -1 \\ -2 & -4 \end{array} \right| + 1 \cdot \left| \begin{array}{cc} 0 & 2 \\ -2 & 4 \end{array} \right| \\[5pt] &= -3( 2\cdot (-4) - 4 \cdot (-1) ) - 3(0\cdot (-4) - (-2)\cdot (-1)) + (0\cdot 4 - (-2)\cdot 2) \\[5pt] &= 12 + 6 + 4 \\[5pt] &= 22. \end{align*}

Therefore, the volume of the corresponding parallelpiped spanned by $\overrightarrow{AB},$ $\overrightarrow{AC},$ and $\overrightarrow{AD}$ is

\[ V = |22| = 22. \]

question.text: Calculate the volume $V$ of the parallelepiped spanned by $\overrightarrow{AB},$ $\overrightarrow{AC},$ and $\overrightarrow{AD},$ given the points $A(1,0,2),$ $B(3,4,5),$ $C(6,2,4),$ and $D(5,3,6).$
question.explanation:
First, we find the displacement vectors $\overrightarrow{AB},$ $\overrightarrow{AC},$ and $\overrightarrow{AD}$ that span the parallelepiped:

\begin{align*} \overrightarrow{AB} &= \mathbf{b}-\mathbf{a} \\[3pt] &= (3\mathbf{i}+4\mathbf{j}+5\mathbf{k})-(\mathbf{i}+2\mathbf{k}) \\[3pt] &= 2\mathbf{i}+4\mathbf{j}+3\mathbf{k} \\[3pt] &= \langle 2,4,3 \rangle \\[7pt] \overrightarrow{AC} &= \mathbf{c}-\mathbf{a} \\[3pt] &= (6\mathbf{i}+2\mathbf{j}+4\mathbf{k})-(\mathbf{i}+2\mathbf{k}) \\[3pt] &= 5\mathbf{i}+2\mathbf{j}+2\mathbf{k} \\[3pt] &= \langle 5,2,2 \rangle \\[7pt] \overrightarrow{AD} &= \mathbf{d}-\mathbf{a} \\[3pt] &= (5\mathbf{i}+3\mathbf{j}+6\mathbf{k})-(\mathbf{i}+2\mathbf{k}) \\[3pt] &= 4\mathbf{i}+3\mathbf{j}+4\mathbf{k} \\[3pt] &= \langle 4,3,4 \rangle \end{align*}

Now, to find the volume of the parallelepiped, we need to take the absolute value of the triple product of the above vectors.

Computing the triple product, we have

\begin{align*} \overrightarrow{AB} \cdot (\overrightarrow{AC} \times \overrightarrow{AD}) &= \left| \begin{array}{ccc} 2 & 4 & 3 \\ 5 & 2 & 2 \\ 4 & 3 & 4 \end{array} \right| \\[5pt] &= 2 \cdot \left| \begin{array}{cc} 2 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 \end{array} \right| - 4 \cdot \left| \begin{array}{cc} 5 & 2 \\ 4 & 4 \end{array} \right| + 3 \cdot \left| \begin{array}{cc} 5 & 2 \\ 4 & 3 \end{array} \right| \\[5pt] &= 2(2\cdot 4 - 2 \cdot 3) - 4(5\cdot 4 - 2 \cdot 4) + 3(5\cdot 3 - 2 \cdot 4) \\[5pt] &= 2(8 - 6) - 4(20 - 8) + 3(15 - 8) \\[5pt] &= 4 - 48 + 21 \\[5pt] &= -23. \end{align*}

Therefore, the volume of the corresponding parallelepiped spanned by $\overrightarrow{AB},$ $\overrightarrow{AC},$ and $\overrightarrow{AD}$ is \[ V = |{-23}| = \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{23}. \]

question.text: Calculate the volume $V$ of the parallelepiped spanned by $\overrightarrow{AB},$ $\overrightarrow{AC},$ and $\overrightarrow{AD},$ given the points $A(0,2,-1),$ $B(3,4,1),$ $C(-1,3,2),$ and $D(2,1,0).$
question.explanation:
First, we find the displacement vectors $\overrightarrow{AB},$ $\overrightarrow{AC},$ and $\overrightarrow{AD}$ that span the parallelepiped:

\begin{align*} \overrightarrow{AB} &= \mathbf{b}-\mathbf{a} \\[3pt] &= (3\mathbf{i}+4\mathbf{j}+\mathbf{k})-(2\mathbf{j}-\mathbf{k}) \\[3pt] &= 3\mathbf{i}+2\mathbf{j}+2\mathbf{k} \\[3pt] &= \langle 3,2,2 \rangle \\[7pt] \overrightarrow{AC} &= \mathbf{c}-\mathbf{a} \\[3pt] &= (-\mathbf{i}+3\mathbf{j}+2\mathbf{k})-(2\mathbf{j}-\mathbf{k}) \\[3pt] &= -\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j}+3\mathbf{k} \\[3pt] &= \langle -1,1,3 \rangle \\[7pt] \overrightarrow{AD} &= \mathbf{d}-\mathbf{a} \\[3pt] &= (2\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j})-(2\mathbf{j}-\mathbf{k}) \\[3pt] &= 2\mathbf{i}-\mathbf{j}+\mathbf{k} \\[3pt] &= \langle 2,-1,1 \rangle \end{align*}

Now, to find the volume of the parallelepiped, we need to take the absolute value of the triple product of the above vectors.

Computing the triple product, we have

\begin{align*} \overrightarrow{AB} \cdot (\overrightarrow{AC} \times \overrightarrow{AD}) &= \left| \begin{array}{ccc} 3 & 2 & 2 \\ -1 & 1 & 3 \\ 2 & -1 & 1 \end{array} \right| \\[5pt] &= 3 \cdot \left| \begin{array}{cc} 1 & 3 \\ -1 & 1 \end{array} \right| - 2 \cdot \left| \begin{array}{cc} -1 & 3 \\ 2 & 1 \end{array} \right| + 2 \cdot \left| \begin{array}{cc} -1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 \end{array} \right| \\[5pt] &= 3(1\cdot1 - 3\cdot(-1)) - 2((-1)\cdot1 - 3\cdot2) + 2((-1)\cdot(-1) - 1\cdot2) \\[5pt] &= 3(1 + 3) - 2(-1 - 6) + 2(1 - 2) \\[5pt] &= 12 - (-14) - 2 \\[5pt] &= 24. \end{align*}

Therefore, the volume of the corresponding parallelpiped spanned by $\overrightarrow{AB},$ $\overrightarrow{AC},$ and $\overrightarrow{AD}$ is \[ V = |24| = \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{24}. \]

question.text: Calculate the volume of the parallelepiped spanned by $\overrightarrow{AB}$, $\overrightarrow{AC}$ and $\overrightarrow{AD}$, given the points $A(2,1,2)$, $B(3,3,3)$, $C(-2,-1,3)$, and $D(4,1,4).$
question.explanation:
First, we find the displacement vectors $\overrightarrow{AB},$ $\overrightarrow{AC},$ and $\overrightarrow{AD}$ that span the parallelepiped:

\begin{align*} \overrightarrow{AB} &= \mathbf{b}-\mathbf{a} \\[3pt] &= (3\mathbf{i}+3\mathbf{j}+3\mathbf{k}) - (2\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j}+2\mathbf{k}) \\[3pt] &= \mathbf{i}+2\mathbf{j}+\mathbf{k} \\[3pt] &= \langle 1,2,1 \rangle \\[7pt] \overrightarrow{AC} &= \mathbf{c}-\mathbf{a} \\[3pt] &= (-2\mathbf{i}-\mathbf{j}+3\mathbf{k}) - (2\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j}+2\mathbf{k}) \\[3pt] &= -4\mathbf{i}-2\mathbf{j}+\mathbf{k} \\[3pt] &= \langle -4,-2,1 \rangle \\[7pt] \overrightarrow{AD} &= \mathbf{d}-\mathbf{a} \\[3pt] &= (4\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j}+4\mathbf{k}) - (2\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j}+2\mathbf{k}) \\[3pt] &= 2\mathbf{i}+2\mathbf{k} \\[3pt] &= \langle 2,0,2 \rangle \end{align*}

Now, to find the volume of the parallelepiped, we need to take the absolute value of the triple product of the above vectors.

Computing the triple product, we have

\begin{align*} \overrightarrow{AB} \cdot (\overrightarrow{AC} \times \overrightarrow{AD}) &= \left| \begin{array}{ccc} 1 & 2 & 1 \\ -4 & -2 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & 2 \end{array} \right| \\[5pt] &= 1 \cdot \left| \begin{array}{cc} -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 \end{array} \right| - 2 \cdot \left| \begin{array}{cc} -4 & 1 \\ 2 & 2 \end{array} \right| + 1 \cdot \left| \begin{array}{cc} -4 & -2 \\ 2 & 0 \end{array} \right| \\[5pt] &= ( (-2) \cdot 2 - 0 \cdot 1 ) - 2 ( (-4) \cdot 2 - 2 \cdot 1 ) + ( (-4) \cdot 0 - 2 \cdot (-2) ) \\[5pt] &= -4 +20 +4 \\[5pt] &= 20. \end{align*}

Therefore, the volume of the corresponding parallelpiped spanned by $\overrightarrow{AB},$ $\overrightarrow{AC},$ and $\overrightarrow{AD}$ is

\[ V = |20| = 20. \]
